article.body_html:
An hour after you ride away from the shop, you notice a crack in the mirror housing, a dent in the fairing or a fresh scuff along a side panel. You did not notice it at pickup, and you cannot be sure whether it was already there. The useful move is to report it the same day, with photographs that carry a date and enough detail for the shop to compare them with whatever it has from pickup. This guide covers the first few minutes, the photographs worth taking, what the first message should say and what to ask next.

The first few minutes

  1. Stop somewhere safe before you look at the bike: not in a traffic lane and not on a slope.
  2. Check what you ride with. Do the brakes work normally, does the handlebar turn freely, do the lights and indicators work, are the mirrors tight? A small crack in a plastic panel may be only cosmetic; a loose panel, a bent brake lever or a loose mirror is not. If anything affects control, do not ride on: call the shop.
  3. Photograph before you touch. Wiping off dust or pressing on a crack can change how it looks.
  4. Write down the time and roughly how far you have ridden since pickup.

Photographs that make a report useful

ShotWhat it showsTip
Whole bike, damaged side facing the cameraWhich bike it is and where the damage sitsStep back far enough to include both wheels
Medium shot of the areaThe damage in context: near a footrest, a mirror or a panel edgeHold the camera level, not tilted
Close-upThe size and depth of the markPut a coin or a key beside it for scale
Dashboard with the odometerThe reading at the moment you noticedMake sure the digits are readable
The surroundingsWhere you are, in case the shop asks what happenedA street sign or a shopfront is enough
Your pickup photographs, if you took anyWhat the same spot looked like before you leftSend the matching shot together with the new one

Keep the original files. A phone stores the date and time inside each photograph, and that stored detail is more useful than a screenshot or a forwarded copy. Rental Bike Damage Photos: A Hanoi Handover Shot List lists the angles worth taking at pickup, so that next time the comparison is easier.

What the first message should say

Keep it short, factual and dated. For example: "I collected the [model] at [time] on [date]. At [time], about [number] minutes after leaving, I noticed [a crack / a dent / a scuff] on the [location]. [I did not see it at pickup.] I have attached photographs: the whole bike, the area, a close-up and the odometer. Could you tell me how you would like me to proceed, and whether you have a record of the bike's condition at pickup?" Send it by the channel you used to book, and call the shop at once if brakes, steering or lights are affected.

Why the same day matters

A report sent soon after you noticed the damage is easy to place on a timeline: the bike was collected at one time, the damage was found a short time later, and the distance ridden in between is small. A report sent days later leaves room for other explanations, such as a fall while parked, a knock in a car park or a different rider. That is not a prediction of how the shop will respond. It is a description of why a dated message is easier to work with than an undated memory.

Questions to ask the shop

  • Do you want to see the bike in person, or are the photographs enough for now?
  • Should I keep riding the bike, or bring it back for a check?
  • Is there a record of the bike's condition at pickup that I can compare with my photographs?
  • How would you like the damage noted, and will you confirm it in a message?
  • If a cost may follow, when and how would I be told?

These are questions, not statements about how the shop works. Write down each answer with the time you received it. Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily and can be reached on 0334 699 969; the shop's contact page may list other ways to reach it.

What not to do

  • Do not repair, polish or cover up the mark before the shop has seen it.
  • Do not delete your pickup photographs or the first photographs of the damage, even if they look poor.
  • Do not guess who or what caused it. State what you saw and when.
  • Do not wait until return day in the hope that the mark will not be noticed.

If you took no pickup photographs

Then the comparison rests on your account and on the shop's own record, if it has one. Say so plainly in the message, and photograph the whole bike now in the same careful way, so that anything else you notice later can be dated against these pictures. At return, Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist shows what the receipt should record, and Hanoi Motorbike Rental Deposits: How to Record Payment and Return covers the payment side. Related guides sit in the Booking, Deposits & Handover category.
